turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hi, thanks for coming in today. What's been going on for you lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (sighing slightly) Honestly, everything and nothing? Like I'll be fine and then suddenly I'm thinking about whether I locked the car, or if my mom's flight is going to be okay, or some email I sent three days ago. It's just hard to focus on one thing for too long, you know? (pausing, looking around the room)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I do, yeah. It can be hard to focus on one thing for too long. Have you experienced this a lot lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (shrugging) I'd say it's been going on for a while now. It's just... my mind's always somewhere else. I try to concentrate on work or something, but then I'll start thinking about a bill I need to pay or a favor I need to return to someone. It's like my brain's just constantly jumping from one thing to another. (fidgeting slightly in seat)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That does sound really hard. What do you do to try to cope with it?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looking down, fidgeting with hands) To be honest, I don't really have a good system for coping with it. I try to, you know, take a few deep breaths or go for a walk, but it doesn't really seem to help. Sometimes I'll try to change the subject and think about something else, but then I'll start worrying about that new thing instead. It's just... (pausing, looking up) I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's understandable that you're feeling this way. It can be really tough to deal with. Have you talked to a therapist about this?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (shifting uncomfortably in seat) Oh, no, not really. I mean, I've talked to some friends about it, but... (trailing off) I don't know, I just don't want to be one of those people who's always complaining about their problems. And I don't want to be a burden to anyone. (looking down, fidgeting with hands again) Plus, I don't know if it's really that big of a deal. I mean, I'm not, you know, sleeping on the streets or anything. (nervously chuckling)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That makes sense. It's always a good idea to talk to someone about how you're feeling. If you're not ready to see a therapist yet, that's okay. Maybe you can try talking to a trusted friend or family member about how you're feeling. And if you ever feel like you're in danger, please reach out to a crisis hotline or someone you trust.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (slightly defensive) I said I've talked to friends about it, okay? They just don't get it. They're always like, "Oh, just relax, it's not a big deal." But they don't understand what it's like to be me. (crossing arms) And I'm not in danger or anything. I just... (pausing, looking away) I just wish I could find a way to calm down, you know?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I understand. It can be really difficult to find ways to calm down. Have you tried any specific strategies or techniques?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (shrugging) I try to take deep breaths and stuff, but it doesn't really help. Sometimes I'll try to listen to music or go for a walk, but my mind's always somewhere else. (sighing) And sometimes I'll be doing something calm, like reading a book, and then I'll start worrying about something and it ruins the whole thing. (rubbing temples) I just feel like I'm always on edge, you know? (looking down)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It sounds like you're dealing with a lot. It's okay to feel overwhelmed sometimes. Have you considered seeing a therapist?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looking up, slightly irritated) I already told you, I haven't talked to a therapist about this. And like I said, I'm not sure it's a big deal. I just... (pausing, frowning) I don't know, maybe I'm just fine and I'm overreacting or something. (crossing arms again) But to be honest, just talking about this is making me feel more anxious. Can we talk about something else?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Of course. I'm here to listen. Is there anything else you'd like to talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looking around the room, avoiding eye contact) I don't know... nothing, really. I just... (pausing, looking down) I guess I'm just tired. All this worrying is exhausting. (sighing) Sometimes I feel like my brain is just going to give out or something. (trailing off)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I understand. It's okay to feel exhausted. Have you tried taking breaks or stepping away from things that make you anxious?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (shrugging) I try to, but it's hard to step away from everything. Like, I'll be working on a project and I'll see an email from my boss and I'll start worrying about whether it's good enough, or if I'm going to get yelled at. (rubs temples again) And then I'll try to take a break, but my mind will just start racing with all these other things I need to do. It's like my brain is always on, you know? (sighs)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That can be really hard. It's okay to feel overwhelmed, but it's important to take breaks and give yourself time to relax and focus on one thing at a time. Have you tried any techniques or strategies to help you with that?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (sighs) I try to focus on one thing at a time, but like I said, my mind always jumps to something else. (pauses) I did try to practice some relaxation techniques, like progressive muscle relaxation, but it didn't really work for me. (shrugs) I just feel like my body is always tense, even when I'm not doing anything. (touches shoulders, which are still tense) Like, right now, just thinking about it is making me feel anxious. (looks down, fidgeting with hands)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's okay to feel anxious, but it's important to take care of yourself. Have you tried any physical relaxation techniques, like deep breathing or yoga?
